name: rack-snail-strike
title: Rack Snail Strike
description: A live-count stat tile built on the rack-and-snail striking clock: a stepped spiral cam sets how far a toothed rack drops, then the rack climbs back one tooth per strike, firing a hammer and incrementing the number on every contact — the fall depth IS the count, read out as a sequence of discrete strikes rather than a printed digit.
useWhen: a live count that should read as a mechanical event sequence (one hammer strike per new arrival, cadence a viewer can actually count along with) rather than a smooth or instant number change; pick stat-tile-ascii-arrive instead for a KPI whose number should just visibly resolve out of noise on arrival with no discrete per-unit event, or counter-carry-ripple for a live readout where the STRUCTURE of a multi-digit change (carries rippling right to left) matters more than counting individual arrivals.
instruction: Renders a stat figure driven by the rack-and-snail striking mechanism from English/French striking clocks. A stepped-spiral cam (SVG path, 12 constant radii, one per step 1-12, built once from a closed-form generator — no per-frame trig) rotates under a fixed follower pin over CAM_ROTATE_MS=300ms to select a step; the selected step's radius sets how deep a toothed rack (a DOM row of clipped tooth-shaped spans, its own translateY encoding depth) falls over FALL_MS=400ms with an ease-in transition, depth proportional to the step value (more strikes = falls farther, matching the fixed one-tooth-per-strike gather count — implemented this way rather than the brief's literal (13-stepValue) formula, which contradicted its own 'gathered stepValue times' rule; flagged for spec review). Gathering then runs stepValue times at STRIKE_INTERVAL_MS=850ms per strike: an SVG hammer (a line+circle group pivoting near a bell dome) rotates -34deg away from the bell over LIFT_MS=550ms with an ease-out curve (cocking back), then swings back to 0deg over STRIKE_FALL_MS=150ms on a cubic-bezier(0.3,1.6,0.4,1) curve whose overshoot past 0 IS the strike's bounce (no separate offset needed) — the stat figure increments and gets a 150ms brightness(1.7) luminance flash on --foreground exactly at hammer contact (end of the fall leg), never on lift. Each strike leaves a STRIKE_PAUSE_MS=~150ms gap before the next; after the final strike a rest gap (600-1400ms, longer for low-count steps) precedes the next cam rotation. The idle demo (no `count` prop) loops a fixed non-monotonic sequence [3,7,1,12,5,9] forever via cleared setTimeout chains (no rAF, no continuous painting) so it reads differently at t0/2.5s/5s. Passing a `count` prop disables the idle sequence entirely; the mechanism reacts only to an explicit prop change (one fall-and-gather run per change, clamped 1-12) and never polls a wall clock or infers the real hour. Colour is pure CSS custom-property reference (var(--ns-muted) on cam + rack teeth as structural chrome, var(--foreground) on hammer + bell as the climactic moment, --ns-accent never touched) — no getComputedStyle/MutationObserver needed since SVG/DOM attributes referencing var() repaint for free on a theme class flip. prefers-reduced-motion renders one static frame: the '7' step, 3 of 7 teeth already gathered (rack at a middle fallen depth), hammer resting against the bell having just struck — cam step, rack depth, and hammer-at-bell all legible in one frame, no timers or observers started. Accessible value exposed via a visually-hidden role=status aria-live=polite span. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG only, no canvas.
